summary: CNMD is a profitable, debt-laden specialty-medical-device boring-middle name with PwC as auditor since 1982, no going-concern language, no material weakness, and no activist 13D. The forensic picture is more mixed than a typical pass: (i) the senior credit agreement was amended on July 19, 2024 (4th Amendment) to exclude a $70M convertible-note prepayment from the fixed-charge calculation — a covenant-relief amendment that 'full compliance' framing obscures; (ii) the 2024 reported $132.4M net income embeds $41M of non-cash 'income' from writing down Biorez/In2Bones contingent-consideration liabilities, which the auditor flagged as a Critical Audit Matter — economically this means two recent (2022) acquisitions are missing pro-forma revenue plans; (iii) Q1 2025 operating margin compressed 620bp YoY driven by $12.2M of former-CEO advisory expense (Hartman departed Dec 31, 2024, retained as Special Advisor through March 2027) plus $10.5M unfavorable contingent-consideration swing; (iv) the $800M 2.250% Convertible Notes due 2027 have a $145.32 conversion price vs $57-70 pre-cutoff stock — principal will be refinanced in CASH at materially higher rates; (v) capital-products revenue declined 5.4% CC in FY24 and general-surgery growth halved in Q1 2025, consistent with hospital-capex weakness. Insider behavior shows a 2023 executive sell-cluster (Treasurer/Controller/Counsel sold $7.8M in 3 days at $126+) but ZERO discretionary sales by named officers since May 2024 — pattern is 'sold at the top then quiet,' not active front-running of current distress. Honesty-alpha verdict: framework should NOT short — disclosure quality is good (covenant amendment, advisory cost, write-downs all stated), and there is no going-concern or auditor friction. But this is a tighter pass than most boring-middle names: multiple disclosed-but-pressured items create a leveraged-equity story heading into a 2027 refinancing wall. Leans NEUTRAL with a slight negative tilt.
